sections.h2: Newport News real estate tax rate
sections.html:
The city's assessment history shows a rate of $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26. It has stayed there since 2023-24, after $1.20 in 2021-22 and 2022-23 and $1.22 from 2013-14 through 2020-21. City Council sets the rate, so a complaint about the dollar amount is a conversation with Council, while a complaint about value is an appeal.

Tax yearTotal assessmentRate per $100
2025-26$23,634,402,300$1.18
2024-25$22,686,862,600$1.18
2022-23$20,346,589,500$1.20
2020-21$16,664,512,200$1.22

The city assesses at 100 percent of value every year, and the 2025-26 total is about 4.2 percent above the year before. The Assessor's website has a tax calculator you can use to estimate a bill.

The Real Estate Assessor values each parcel, and the City Treasurer bills and collects. Every parcel is assessed annually, effective the following July 1.

  • Real Estate Assessor: 700 Town Center Drive, Suite 220, phone 757-926-1926, email restate@nnva.gov.
  • Treasurer: P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607, phone 757-926-8731, email treasurer@nnva.gov.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 2400 Washington Avenue, phone 757-926-8752. This office also staffs the Board of Review.

Real estate tax is normally due December 5 and June 5. Improvements made to the land can show up on a supplemental bill. Some bills combine the real estate tax with a stormwater fee, and online bankers should pay the grand total using the account number.

Newport News uses a Board of Review that sits between September 1 and November 30 each year. Applications are accepted from July 1 through September 1, with no extensions. The Newport News Circuit Court judges appoint the Board every year.

  • Weekend deadline: if September 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.
  • Late filings: an application postmarked or hand delivered after the deadline is rejected.
  • Mailing: a USPS postmark now reflects the day the mail was processed, which can be later than the day you dropped it off. Hand delivery or an early mailing is safer.
  • Questions: call the Board's administrative assistant at 757-812-7816.

Residential and commercial appeals use separate forms. If someone files for you, the city also provides a letter of authorization for agents.

If your value jumped, ask the Assessor for a review before the September 1 deadline arrives. A review is a chance to check the square footage, condition and sales the city used.

Newport News sits at the southeastern end of the Virginia Peninsula, on the north shore of the James River where it meets Hampton Roads. The 2020 census counted 186,247 residents. Some neighborhoods lie in what used to be the City of Warwick, which merged with Newport News in 1958, so an address can carry a different history than a neighbor a few miles away.

Water covers 42 percent of the city's area. A seller should expect buyers to ask whether a house is near a creek, a river inlet or a mapped flood zone, so find your flood zone before you list. A copy of any elevation certificate you already have will answer most of those questions in one step.

The city has dozens of named neighborhoods, from the planned community of Hilton Village in the south to Denbigh in the north. Others include Oyster Point, City Center, Port Warwick, Lee Hall, Riverside, Menchville, Windsor Great Park and the East End. Port Warwick and City Center at Oyster Point came from New Urbanism projects that began in the early 2000s, so houses and condos in them have a different feel and age than the older streets in the East End.

Interstates 64 and 664 and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel link the city to the rest of Hampton Roads, and the airport is inside city limits.

Virginia law puts a tax lien on the real estate ahead of any other lien, so delinquent tax is paid from the sale proceeds. Under Va. Code 58.1-3340, the buyer, or the trustee at a foreclosure sale, must apply proceeds to taxes and levies, penalties and interest included, and the treasurer then releases the lien.

The seller's liability for the year is prorated by contract, so the sale agreement should say who pays the current half. Va. Code 58.1-802 adds a state and local grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of price. The seller pays it unless the parties arrange otherwise, and the circuit court clerk collects it at recording.

The Treasurer also keeps a page for real estate auctions of properties with delinquent taxes or liens, with the legal notice and an auction flyer. An owner who sees a notice for their own parcel has little time left to choose the terms of a sale.

sections.h2: Relief programs for owners behind on tax
sections.html:
The Commissioner of the Revenue runs several relief programs: a real estate tax deferral for the elderly and disabled, an exemption for disabled former service members, and mobile home deferral and exemption programs. A Residential Rehabilitation Property Tax Abatement Program has its own calculator, and the Assessor's site offers a VA Deed Alert tool. Income limits and rules sit on each program's page. Call 757-926-8653 with state income and tax relief questions.

If no program fits and the house needs more work than you can fund, a cash sale as is can clear the tax at closing instead.

Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff in advance. Confirm whether the December 5 or June 5 installment is still open, and whether a supplemental bill or a stormwater charge is on the account. Give the figure to your title company so the lien can be released the day the deed is recorded.

  • Bring the account number and the parcel address to the Treasurer's office or have them ready on the phone.
  • Check the sale agreement to see who covers the current half year.
  • Look at the Assessor's website for the improvements on record, since added work can change the bill.
  • If a notice of auction shows up for your parcel, call the Treasurer the same day to ask what it takes to stop the sale.
  • Tell the buyer or the agent early if you are appealing, so the closing date does not collide with a Board of Review hearing.

A cash buyer can close on whatever schedule suits you once the payoff is known, which helps when a bill is already late or a hearing is coming.

faqs.q: What is the Newport News property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26, the same as 2024-25 and 2023-24. City Council sets the rate each year, so confirm it with the Assessor or Treasurer.

faqs.q: When are Newport News real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: They are normally due December 5 and June 5. Improvements to the land may be billed on a supplemental bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Newport News assessment?
faqs.a: Applications to the Board of Review are accepted July 1 through September 1, with no extensions. If September 1 is a weekend or holiday, the next business day is the deadline.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Newport News Treasurer?
faqs.a: Mail goes to P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607. Call 757-926-8731 or email treasurer@nnva.gov. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Newport News house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia's tax lien comes first, so the title company pays the balance from your proceeds and the treasurer releases the lien. Ask for a written payoff amount before closing.
